evidence.quote: A 28-year-old woman was admitted with HBsAg positivity for 6 days and abnormal liver function tests for 1 day.
This case series reports three pregnant women with acute hepatitis B virus (AHB) infection, exploring their clinical outcomes and comorbid anxiety.

Two weeks after admission, HBsAg became negative. HBcAb IgM became undetectable by day 50, and anti-HBs appeared more than seven months later. HBV DNA clearance was synchronized with HBsAg seroconversion. Liver function normalized and remained stable during one year of follow-up.

She had undergone hospitalization in the gynecology department for a missed abortion 6 days earlier, during which hepatitis B serology revealed HBsAg >250.00 IU/mL, hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) 55.719 S/CO, hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) 3.42 S/CO, and IgM antibody against HBcAg (HBcAb-IgM) 0.07 S/CO.

Her past medical history included a dental procedure two months prior. She denied blood transfusions, other surgeries, or known HBV infection. Obstetric history included gravida 3, para 1, with two induced abortions. Her last menstrual period was December 29, 2016. She denied unsafe sexual contact. Her husband and son were negative for hepatitis B markers, and there was no family history of HBV.

claims.text: A 28-year-old woman had incident HBsAg positivity during admission for missed abortion, initially with normal liver function and CBC, followed by D&C on day −2 with degenerated villous tissue. Her recorded G3P1 and two induced abortions have unclear counting scope. A dental procedure two months earlier was reported without a proven transmission link; transfusions, other surgery, prior known HBV and unsafe sexual contact were denied. Family HBV history was negative, and husband/son markers were negative. Admission was asymptomatic apart from mild scleral icterus. HBV DNA was 2600 IU/ml, ALT 3657/AST 1849 U/L, bilirubin 42.1 μmol/L and platelets 51 ×10⁹/L. Other viral/autoantibody studies were negative; ultrasound found a hepatic cyst and chronic cholecystitis. Compound glycyrrhizin, reduced glutathione and adenosylmethionine were given without antivirals. Thrombocytopenia reached 43 ×10⁹/L without significant bleeding and resolved after monitoring without intervention. Table HBsAg was negative on day 10; the narrative describes negativity around two weeks. Disease-course durations are reported with a separate origin and are not assigned admission-day timestamps. HBcAb IgM became negative by day 50 and anti-HBs appeared after seven months; liver function remained normal through one year. Persistent depressed mood, work concentration difficulty and author-reported anxiety were assessed qualitatively.

claims.text: A 23-year-old woman at eight weeks gestation presented with two weeks of greasy-food aversion and one week of fatigue. Gravida 0 was recorded despite current pregnancy; LMP was April 12, 2018. Transfusions, surgery, prior HBV and high-risk sexual behavior were denied, with negative family history. Examination and admission CBC were normal. HBsAg was 44.45 IU/ml, HBcAb IgM 2.08 S/CO, ALT 512/AST 445 U/L, bilirubin 15 μmol/L and β-hCG 2057.4 IU/L. Ultrasound confirmed intrauterine pregnancy and a hyperechoic hepatic nodule consistent with possible hemangioma. Other viral/autoantibody panels were negative. Compound glycyrrhizin was given without antivirals. HBsAg became negative and anti-HBs positive by day 6; ALT/AST normalized by day 14 and HBV DNA was <30 IU/ml at one month. Anti-HBs was negative at Month 1+ and positive again at Month 3+/4+. Liver function remained normal through six months. Month 4+ IgM positivity is retained after earlier negativity without inferring reactivation. Marked anxiety about liver failure/fetal harm persisted despite repeated reassurance. Systematic mental-health protocols were not implemented; pregnancy outcome is unreported. Early-course HBV DNA was 180 IU/mL; its day 0 versus day 2 timing is unresolved.

claims.text: A 25-year-old woman at ten weeks gestation had week-long dizziness/fatigue and one day of low-grade fever and generalized pruritic rash, with mild icterus and upper-limb erythematous eruptions. Gravida 0 was recorded despite current pregnancy; LMP was March 20, 2018. Prior HBV, transfusions, surgery, high-risk sexual behavior and family HBV history were denied; pre-pregnancy HBsAg was negative. Admission ALT was 1798/AST 1508 U/L and bilirubin 51.8 μmol/L. Day 1 HBsAg was >250 IU/ml, HBcAb IgM 22.27 S/CO and DNA 7.8 million IU/ml. PT was mildly prolonged without encephalopathy; initial CBC was normal and hepatic echogenicity slightly increased. Other viral panels were negative. AMA-M2 positivity raised possible PBC, which remained unevaluated. Ultrasound confirmed viable intrauterine pregnancy. Compound glycyrrhizin, polyenylphosphatidylcholine and adenosylmethionine were given without antivirals. HBsAg cleared and anti-HBs appeared by day 5; by day 15 anti-HBs was negative and DNA remained 1900 IU/ml despite marked biochemical improvement. She was lost to follow-up, so full DNA clearance, PBC and obstetric outcomes remain unknown despite broad abstract cure wording. Profound anxiety and repeated reassurance requests were documented qualitatively.

source_evidence.quote: A 25-year-old woman at 10 weeks of gestation presented with one week of dizziness and fatigue, accompanied by low-grade fever and a generalized pruritic rash for one day.
This case series reports three pregnant women with acute hepatitis B virus (AHB) infection, exploring their clinical outcomes and comorbid anxiety.
Past medical history was unremarkable; she denied transfusions, surgery, or prior HBV infection.
Autoantibody screening revealed anti-mitochondrial antibody M2 positivity, raising the possibility of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), though no follow-up evaluation was completed.
